question: How many astronomical observatories were constructed by Sawai Jai Singh, the ruler of Amber?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Sawai Jai Singh II**, the ruler of Amber (later Jaipur), was a renowned astronomer and mathematician who constructed **five astronomical observatories**, known as **Jantar Mantars**, in different parts of India.

• The observatories were established in the cities of **Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi**.

• These observatories were built during the early 18th century, between **1724 and 1734**, under Sawai Jai Singh's supervision.

• The purpose of these observatories was to make **accurate astronomical measurements**, aid in the preparation of astrological charts, and improve the study of celestial movements.

• The most prominent of these observatories is the **Jantar Mantar in Jaipur**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site and contains the world's largest stone sundial, known as the **Samrat Yantra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Architectural Significance:**

• The observatories are known for their unique and innovative **architectural designs**, combining science and aesthetics.

• Each Jantar Mantar includes several instruments made of stone and brass, such as **sundials, astrolabes, and quadrants**, which were used for astronomical calculations.

• **Scientific Contributions:**

• Sawai Jai Singh II was inspired by **Islamic and European astronomical techniques**, such as those of Ptolemy and Ulugh Beg.

• He compiled the **Zij-i Muhammad Shahi**, an astronomical table based on observations from his observatories and earlier works.

• **Preservation of Observatories:**

• Most of the observatories have been preserved, with **Jaipur's Jantar Mantar** being the most well-maintained and popular among tourists.

• The Jantar Mantars are recognized as historical landmarks and represent India's rich scientific heritage.

• **Decline of Mathura Observatory:**

• The Jantar Mantar in Mathura has been lost due to neglect and urban development, leaving only four of the original five observatories intact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **UNESCO Recognition:**

• The Jantar Mantar in Jaipur was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2010** for its cultural and scientific significance.

• **Legacy:**

• Sawai Jai Singh II's efforts in astronomy exemplify India's contributions to science and mathematics during the **Mughal period**.
